review.issue: The draft's rationale for the first idea asserts that an expectation‑setting piece is 'likely to address the main barrier signalled in the source,' which reads as a causal claim. The source reports that 'welcome' was the most‑cited return reason and that the committee kept a later entry window, but it does not provide evidence that an expectation‑setting notice will reduce hesitation or increase attendance.
review.sourceEvidence: After the October rehearsal, twelve of the nineteen people present answered a short question about returning. Eight mentioned the welcome, three mentioned the songs, and one mentioned both. Two people who had missed the previous rehearsal said late trains had played a part. The choir agreed at its monthly meeting to keep the later entry window through December. The minutes record the decision without an account of why it was chosen. There has been no survey of confidence before and after singing and no comparison with a fixed-start rehearsal.

ideas.title: A step‑by‑step 'What to expect on your first Wednesday' guide to help hesitant adults decide to try the taster
ideas.description: A short, vividly practical piece that walks a hesitant adult through the actual evening: who is invited, no auditions/no need to read music, the shared warm‑up with an option to listen, the 19:00 start and quiet entry until 19:20, and the free first taster with normal contribution from visit two — written to reduce uncertainty and lower the barrier to attend.
ideas.audience: Adults who are unsure about singing in a group and are weighing whether to attend a one‑off taster
ideas.rationale: The notice's stated purpose is to help a hesitant newcomer 'picture the evening', and informal rehearsal feedback emphasised the choir's welcome and a later entry window — together these make an expectation‑setting guide a plausible, directly relevant way to reduce uncertainty, while recognising the source provides no causal evidence that this will increase attendance.
ideas.evidence: Source provides the taster details (who's invited, practical arrangements and free first visit), the short rehearsal feedback showing welcome as the top return reason, the committee decision to keep a later entry window, and an explicit statement that there has been no formal survey of confidence or a fixed‑start comparison.

ideas.title: Brief internal report for the choir committee summarising rehearsal feedback and the decision to keep the later‑entry window
ideas.description: A concise two‑panel memo: (1) document the October micro‑survey counts (12 answered; 8 cited welcome, 3 songs, 1 both; two missed due to late trains), (2) note the committee decision to retain later entry through December and that minutes record the decision without explaining why, (3) flag gaps in evidence (no confidence survey, no fixed‑start comparison).
ideas.audience: Choir committee and volunteer organisers who make access and scheduling decisions
ideas.rationale: The rehearsal responses and the recorded committee decision are present in the source; packaging those facts and the recorded evidence gaps will support clearer governance and any future, justified operational choices.
ideas.evidence: The source lists the micro‑survey counts and reasons given by members, records the committee decision to keep the later entry window, and explicitly states there has been no survey comparing confidence or fixed‑start rehearsals.
